title: One job, many permits
question: How many separate permits, from how many departments, does one ordinary job need?
finding: A finished home remodel costing $100,000 to $1 million carried a median 7 separate permits and records from 4 departments, and took a median 565 days from first filing to final sign-off, building time included; one in ten carried 17 or more. A new building with five or more homes carried a median 45 permits and records across 6 departments and took 6.2 years.
how: For each finished job filed 2015 to 2023 (the largest building permit on the lot in its window), every record on the same lot between 30 days before filing and final sign-off was counted: other building permits (revisions, separate permits for sprinklers, shoring, demolition and the like), separate electrical and plumbing permits, Public Works street permits that quote the job's permit number or address, and the Planning project record with its attached reviews. Departments are those that appear in the plan-review routing or issued one of these permits.
limits: Some of the stack is the owner's choice (splitting work into phases, filing revisions). A lot can hold unrelated work, so the count is restricted to houses and new buildings and to the largest job in each window; restaurants share buildings with other tenants and may be overcounted. Fire, health and entertainment operating permits are not linked by lot and are left out, so the true stack is larger. Private homes are not listed; the worst cases are shown by type and neighborhood only.
